newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger opposition given more time for election.
newsitem.headline: Niger opposition given more time for election.

text.p: Niger's government extended the deadline for candidates to register for legislative elections and has resumed talks with the main opposition parties to persuade them to take part in the November polls.

A government statement issued on Friday said the two sides were discussing ways of achieving consensus on the organisation of the November 23 election and that candidates now had until the end of the day on October 28 to register.
Talks between the two sides broke down on October 11.

Opposition parties, angry over the conduct of the July presidential election won by coup maker Ibrahim Bare Mainassara, let Wednesday's previous deadline pass without registering and without naming representatives to a new electoral commission.

The November 23 election of the 83 members of the new national assembly is part of Mainassara's efforts to return the mainly Moslem West African state to multi-party politics following his coup in January.
Mainassara, who toppled an elected president and government, scrapped the independent national electoral commission part way through the presidential election.
Eight opposition parties, grouped in the Front for the Restoration and Defence of Democracy, are demanding that the old electoral commission be restored.
Further demands include reconstituted constitutional and supreme courts and U.N., Organisation of African Unity and European Union supervision of all Niger elections.
